# Appendix F — Security Requirements Baseline

This baseline consolidates security requirements that enterprise customers commonly place on suppliers and that organizations apply to their own solutions. Use it in two directions: to assess a supplier or SaaS product, and to check that a solution offered to customers can meet typical contractual expectations. Requirements are generalized; actual contracts may be stricter. Each row names the architecture evidence that demonstrates the requirement and the main reference. Frequencies such as “annually” are common contractual defaults, not universal requirements: apply the interval the contract, regulation or risk assessment sets. The coverage map in F.1 links each baseline table to the handbook sections, and the editions cited are listed at the end (F.10). Each section holds one table with the same number: the access-control section (F.4), for example, contains Table F.4.

## F.2 Governance, Assurance and Audit

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Maintain a security program aligned with recognized standards, owned by an accountable security leader and reviewed annually | Program documentation; named accountable owner | ISO/IEC 27001:2022; NIST CSF 2.0 |
| Assess risks to customer data and systems at least annually | Risk assessment with treatment plan | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Provide independent assurance for restricted data | SOC 1 Type II report (financial-reporting controls) or SOC 2 Type II report (an attestation that controls operated over a period), or ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification (of the management system) whose scope includes the service; these are not equivalent, and a customer may require one specifically | AICPA Trust Services Criteria; ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Provide PCI DSS evidence when handling cardholder data | Attestation of Compliance and responsibility matrix | PCI DSS v4.0.1 |
| Permit audits and share relevant audit findings | Audit clause; evidence repository; control matrix | Contract; 4.9 |
| Keep a tamper-evident audit trail of privileged actions and access to customer data | Audit-event catalog; protected audit store | 13.7.2 |

: Governance, assurance and audit requirements

## F.3 Third Parties and Personnel

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Assess and monitor material subcontractors annually; disclose subprocessors | Supplier register with risk tier and review dates | ISO/IEC 27001:2022; 13.8 |
| Train personnel with data or system access in security annually | Training records | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |
| Screen personnel before granting access | Background-check records, subject to local law | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |

: Third-party and personnel requirements

## F.4 Access Control and Identity

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Use strong authentication, with MFA for all remote and privileged access | IdP policy; MFA coverage report | NIST SP 800-63-4 (2025); 13.2.2 |
| Grant access on business need; review periodically; revoke promptly | Access-review records; automated deprovisioning | 13.2.1; 13.3 |
| Protect remote connections with encryption and network access control | VPN or zero-trust access design | NIST SP 800-207; 13.4.1 |
| Control mobile access to data with mobile device and application management | Mobile device and application management policy | Organizational policy |
| Support customer SSO (SAML 2.0 or OIDC) for cloud services | SSO configuration per tenant; SCIM provisioning | 13.2.3 |
| Secure programmatic access with tokens or certificates that are rotated regularly | Workload identity design; rotation evidence | 13.2.5 |

: Access control and identity requirements

## F.5 System Security

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Apply a formal change control process | Change records and approval model | 15.4 |
| Use anti-malware or endpoint detection and response, firewalls and intrusion detection or prevention | Control inventory per environment | NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (2020) |
| Harden and securely configure systems | Configuration baselines; configuration scanning | CIS Benchmarks; 13.5.3 |
| Scan for vulnerabilities periodically and remediate by criticality | Vulnerability register; remediation metrics | 13.6 |
| Patch firmware, operating systems, middleware and applications | Patch policy with risk-based timelines | 13.6.3 |
| Penetration-test externally accessible systems at least annually | Test report and retest | 13.5.5 |
| Log, monitor and respond to security events continuously | Monitoring design; on-call coverage | 13.7.1 |

: System security requirements

## F.6 Data Protection

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Segregate customer data from other customers and environments | Tenancy and environment design | 13.4.3 |
| Encrypt data in transit (TLS 1.2 minimum, 1.3 preferred) and restricted data at rest, including backups | Encryption design; configuration evidence | 13.4.2 |
| Protect encryption keys against unauthorized access and loss | Key-management design; key-access audit | 13.4.2 |
| Separate production from test and development; use masked or synthetic test data | Environment design; data-masking procedure | 13.4.3 |
| Log access to customer data and retain logs (commonly at least one year) | Logging design and retention configuration | 9.2.4, 13.7.2 |
| Prohibit restricted data on removable media and unapproved cloud services | Data-loss prevention and policy controls | Organizational policy |
| Back up data to meet agreed RTO and RPO | Backup design; restore test results | 1.2.10; 12.4 |
| Return or securely destroy data at contract end, with a certificate of destruction | Data export capability; sanitization procedure | NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 (2025) |
| Assess privacy risk before high-risk processing goes live | DPIA with mitigations and a residual-risk owner | GDPR Article 35; 13.9.2 |
| Fulfill data-subject requests within statutory deadlines | Subject-data locator, export and erasure procedures; request log | GDPR Articles 15–22; 13.9.3 |
| Disclose data locations and subprocessors; use a lawful mechanism for cross-border transfers | Data-flow map; transfer register | GDPR Chapter V; 13.9.5 |

: Data protection requirements

## F.7 Application Security

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Train developers in secure development; follow secure coding standards | Training records; coding standards | OWASP; SEI CERT |
| Meet an agreed OWASP ASVS level for applications handling customer data | ASVS level in requirements; verification coverage report | OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 (2025); 13.5.2 |
| Threat-model applications and systems | Threat models per release | 13.1.1 |
| Perform static source code analysis | SAST results in the pipeline | 13.5.3 |
| Perform software composition analysis | SCA results; SBOM | 13.5.3; 13.5.6 |
| Perform authenticated dynamic web application security scans | Authenticated DAST reports | 13.5.4 |
| Perform penetration tests | Penetration-test report with retest | 13.5.5 |
| Notify customers of vulnerabilities with their CVSS rating | Disclosure procedure; advisories with vector strings | 13.6 |

: Application security requirements

## F.8 Cloud Services

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Document the shared responsibility model and recommended secure configuration | Customer-facing security documentation | Chapter 12 |
| Integrate with the customer’s SSO | SAML 2.0 or OIDC support | 13.2.3 |
| Maintain an inventory of cloud identities and account or tenant mappings | Cloud identity inventory; account and tenant map | 13.2.1; 12.1.1 |
| Provide access logs to the customer in real time or near real time | Log export or streaming interface | 13.7.2 |
| Delete personal data when no longer required; export all customer data at contract end | Deletion and export capabilities | 9.2.4; 13.9 |

: Cloud service requirements

## F.9 Business Continuity and Incident Management

| Requirement | Architecture evidence | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Maintain BCP and DRP, updated and tested at least annually | Plans and exercise reports | ISO 22301:2019; 12.4.3 |
| Document RTO and RPO in the service agreement | Service agreement; recovery design | 1.2.10 |
| Report security incidents affecting the customer within the agreed deadline (commonly 24–48 hours) | Incident procedure with notification step | 13.7.3 |
| Provide a security contact and deliver a corrective plan after an incident | Contact register; post-incident action plan | 13.7.3, 14.5.2 |
| Restrict physical access to systems and media | Facility controls, or provider attestation for cloud | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 |

: Business continuity and incident management requirements
